do.name: Walking the old town and Petite Venise
do.detail: Half timbered streets survived the wars intact, and the Lauch canals behind the old tanners quarter carry flowers all summer.

do.name: Unterlinden Museum and the Isenheim altarpiece
do.detail: A former convent holds Grunewald's altarpiece, opened out panel by panel, alongside Upper Rhine painting and a modern wing.

do.name: Tasting along the Alsace wine route
do.detail: Colmar sits mid route, so cellars in Riquewihr, Kaysersberg and Ribeauville are a short bus or bike ride for Riesling and Gewurztraminer.

do.name: Flat bottomed boat ride through Little Venice
do.detail: A short punt along the Lauch from the fishmongers quay, passing back gardens and low bridges at water level.

do.name: Bartholdi Museum, home of the Statue of Liberty sculptor
do.detail: The sculptor was born in this house, and the rooms hold his models and drawings for the statue and for Colmar's own fountains.

do.name: Maison des Tetes and the Pfister house
do.detail: The two show houses of the old town, one hung with over a hundred carved faces, the other with a painted corner turret. Both are a few steps off the market square.

do.name: Colmar Christmas markets
do.detail: Six markets fill the squares from late November to the end of December, with a wheel, lit facades and mulled wine cellars.

do.name: Foire aux Vins d'Alsace
do.detail: The region's biggest fair runs about a fortnight each August, pairing growers' tastings with a run of evening concerts.
